piece: Chopin, Scherzo No. 3 (owner-provided identification). Second-half recording: scherzo3_2.mp3.
art_notes:
Begin with a fragile, nearly extinguished candle in a dark church, with minor-key solemnity reminiscent of a funeral march. "Funeral march" describes the atmosphere, not a different composition.

Revision explicitly requested by the owner in the Codex chat on 2026-11-01:
- After the music turns to the major mode, let the flame grow in response to the performed crescendo.
- At the start of the passage in octaves in both hands, let the church collapse and reveal another world.
- Use the fast passages to open up and move into that otherworld.
- The owner selected a violent world of flames, rocks and a storm.

Additional ending revision explicitly requested by the owner in the Codex chat on 2026-11-01:
- After the very last ascending scale, let the storm clouds part and clear for the ending.

Preserve the original performance. Determine event positions automatically from the recording and, if validated, alignment with the musical score; do not enter source seconds manually or impose a fixed BPM. Preserve the concluding coda. Treat musical interpretation separately from timing precision. Produce this separately from the first-half work.

creative_brief.world: An imagined dark chapel opens into a violent world of fire, basalt rock and storm; not the actual recording venue.
creative_brief.character: One fragile candle, then falling masonry and an open molten landscape; no people.
creative_brief.narrative_arc: The candle barely survives in the dark nave, then grows with the performed crescendo after the major arrival. Both-hands octaves fracture the church and fast passages enter a violent fire, basalt and storm world. After the final long ascending scale reaches its high point, the storm parts progressively into open blue sky and golden light while the original concluding coda continues.
creative_brief.creative_interpretation: The owner supplied the solemn opening, crescendo, octave collapse, violent world and victorious coda; signal activity alone is not interpreted as emotion.

scene_guidance.direction: A nearly extinguished candle in a solemn, dark nave.
scene_guidance.composition: Keep the wick readable and slowly approach the candle.
scene_guidance.palette_intent: Charcoal/indigo candlelight becomes incandescent lava, dark basalt and storm-blue cloud.

scene_guidance.direction: The flame grows with the performed crescendo after the major arrival.
scene_guidance.composition: Keep flame, wick and surrounding cast light attached in one frame.
scene_guidance.palette_intent: Charcoal/indigo candlelight becomes incandescent lava, dark basalt and storm-blue cloud.

scene_guidance.direction: At both-hands octaves, turn and drop the chapel image fragments to expose the fire,basalt and storm world; enter it at the fast coda. After the final ascent, let banks recede and thin cloud remnants into wisps for an open blue/golden ending.
scene_guidance.composition: Preserve the central lava route and the original rock silhouettes as the sky opens.
scene_guidance.palette_intent: Storm blue and incandescent lava give way to spacious pale blue and warm golden sky.

creative_brief.renderer_constraints: Use registered candle-clearing-v1 with chopin-scherzo3-coda-clearing-v1. Preserve original performance and native source samples. Clearing starts at the first frame boundary at or after its detected source sample. Cloud bank interiors retain painted detail; thin lobes and fragments lose opacity continuously without hard opaque chips or a broad gray veil. Preserve the native rock/sky matte. No manual recording seconds,fixed BPM,per-note cuts or generated audio. At clearing activation begin with small source-textured fissures and grow continuously into the established recession. No bulk blue aperture or bright horizon replacement on the cue frame; preserve the same180-frame endpoint.
